assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a general, ligand-tunable reaction. It is used daily across pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis, and it is the kind of enabling methodology that shortens routes and improves efficiency in synthesis. The ligand-design logic (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkyl phosphines) is a clear conceptual advance.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the general, catalytic, practical versions with complementary ligand classes and mechanistic work. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling and Migita-type precedent are real but were stoichiometric in tin and narrow, so I would not include him. A two-person prize seems fair, though precedence will be argued.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent use and confirmation, and mechanisms are well understood. Timing is not premature. The residual issue is the shadow of the 2010 cross-coupling prize, not the maturity of the science.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Precedence for Kosugi/Migita and the Guram/Rennels contributions is from my memory and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating ubiquitous C-H bonds as functional groups. Directing-group and ligand-accelerated Pd chemistry, including remote and meta selective variants, delivers site selectivity that is central to step-economy in total synthesis and late-stage diversification. The impact on how complex molecules are planned is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many groups (Yu, Sanford, Hartwig, Daugulis, Smith). Yu is the clearest leader in ligand and template control of selectivity and Sanford in Pd(II/IV) and fluorination-type transformations. Hartwig's borylation and Smith's work are real but are better set aside here, since Hartwig also appears on B046. Allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Active field, widely reproduced, with steady uptake in industry. Some of the newest template/remote methods are still maturing, so the prize might be a few years early compared with the C-N coupling.
uncertainties: Boundaries between this and Bergman's alkane activation (B026) and Hartwig's borylation are blurred.
Practical scale-up and scope of the most recent ligand-enabled methods remain uneven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides in water, enabling total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins with defined modifications. It is a conceptually clean chemoselective reaction that opened up protein chemistry to synthetic design and enabled work on post-translational modification, D-proteins and ion channels.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed the original NCL (with Dawson, Muir, Clark-Lewis, Kent, 1994) and Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu made major downstream contributions but the core idea and its extension are best captured by these three.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of broad confirmation and use. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Relative priority of Kent versus Dawson and the role of Danishefsky's glycoprotein syntheses is debatable.
Practical impact on drug manufacture is smaller than the chemical-biology impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues convert small molecules into tools that remove proteins, creating a new pharmacological modality. The thalidomide-cereblon mechanism gives a strong molecular-level story, and degraders are now in clinical trials. The chemistry-driven concept is original and has broad consequences for drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Gray and others made key advances (VHL ligands, degrader design). The credit is large and entangled, which is a real problem for a three-person cap.
assessment.maturity: Fast-moving, with many clinical programs but no approved PROTAC drug as far as I know. Possibly premature, although the molecular-glue part is better established.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete and could change the perceived importance.
Which of the PROTAC concept, the cereblon mechanism and the clinical molecular glues deserves recognition is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids in living cells, so chemists can design protein structure at the atomic level. It is a general, original technology widely used for probes, crosslinkers and therapeutics, and Chin's work extends it to quadruplet codons and orthogonal ribosomes.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the in vivo methodology; Chin made decisive contributions to multiple-site and orthogonal-ribosome systems; Yokoyama, Wang and Mehl also contributed significantly. Two names capture the principal conceptual line, but the choice is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of independent use. Mature, though the most powerful extensions are still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the biology-oriented genetic code literature and with the NCL candidate in protein chemistry.
Allocation among Schultz, Wang, Yokoyama and Chin is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry is the chemical basis for routine automated oligonucleotide synthesis, which supports PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide drugs. The reaction design (stable P(III) amidites, tetrazole activation, protecting-group strategy) is an elegant synthetic solution with large and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and the solid-phase automated cycle; Hood is credited here for automated instrumentation, which is more technological. A single laureate would be defensible, though Beaucage's role and prior phosphite-triester work by Letsinger are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, over 40 years, and arguably recognised late. Timing is not a concern but the novelty relative to the recent Nobel record in nucleic-acid tools is.
uncertainties: Omission of Beaucage, Letsinger and Matteucci from the credited names is a fairness concern I cannot fix within the list.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as enabling technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis gives mild single-electron pathways for bond formation, and merged with other catalysts it has expanded reaction types in medicinal chemistry. The scope is large and uptake in industry is wide. Conceptually the radical/SET manifold is less new than the impact suggests.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz and MacMillan reported the key 2008-2011 synthetic reports; MacMillan was already recognised (organocatalysis, 2021) so I avoid him. Konig, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre also have claims. This is a crowded and difficult credit.
assessment.maturity: Fast-growing and well reproduced, but some reproducibility, scalability and mechanistic issues remain, and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among seven names is hard and the earlier Ru/Ir photochemistry is not credited.
Whether the field is mature enough or whether durable conceptual novelty beyond the SET manifold is established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable carbenes (imidazolylidenes and cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) revealed that these species can be bottled, and they became ubiquitous ligands for metathesis and cross-coupling and organocatalysts. The conceptual shift in main-group and organometallic bonding is significant.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first stable crystalline NHC in 1991; Bertrand isolated the earlier phosphinocarbene (1988) and later CAACs. Nolan and Rovis are important for applications and catalysis; including them would dilute the discovery attribution.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed. Some of the impact is already recognised through the 2005 metathesis prize, which reduces urgency.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 metathesis prize in terms of the impact narrative.
Priority between Bertrand's 1988 species and Arduengo's 1991 NHC may be argued.
